creator: Akshat Shrivastava
source_note: Detailed summary generated from the video's English auto-captions; figures are as Akshat states them on screen (some are garbled by auto-captions, e.g. gold's fall is given as both 38% and 40% in different places).
summary: Akshat Shrivastava argues the US market's ~20-22% correction is a buying opportunity, not the AI bubble bursting, and says he has been buying aggressively and will buy more next week. His first argument is about shape: 2022 was a W-shaped correction that took two years to recover, while the July 2024 dip (~17%), the 2025 dips (12-13% and ~20%) and the current one all look V-shaped, so buying the dip should pay off quickly if this one is V-shaped too. Second, he says it is a valuation correction, not a bubble burst: in a real burst money flees to safety, but gold has corrected ~38-40% (more than the Nasdaq) and money is not rotating into the Indian market either — Nifty has not even recovered its 2024 peak. He blames the sell-off largely on unwound leverage: 3x levered positions turned a 5% fall into 15%, forced liquidations followed, and he cites a young fund manager's 'situational awareness fund' losing ~95%. On valuation, S&P 500 forward PE is 16.7 against a 10-year average of 19.1, QQQ is 18.7 against 22, and Nifty is at fair value (~18.9 vs 18.8), with S&P/QQQ EPS growth of ~16-20% still intact and no earnings slowdown signalled — Nvidia's latest call gave good guidance. At stock level Nvidia's PEG is 0.15 after a ~50% correction from the top, Google is 35-40% down, and Microsoft, Meta and Amazon have all corrected. He also explains gold's fall: the Fed is raising rates, US bonds pay ~5-5.5% and Dubai bank FDs ~6% in dollars, so gold competes with bonds, not equities — and bond money gets lent on to AI capex, which is what keeps US GDP positive. His action plan: buy indices now — QQQ and S&P 500 are the two best, SOXX only if you want extra volatility — and wait for the market to consolidate before rotating into individual stocks. He puts the maximum fall around QQQ 550-560, roughly 30-35% from the peak. On Nvidia's Jensen Huang case and accounting questions, he says the news looks concerted, the government will do everything to save AI companies, and he is not scared as long as Nvidia is not a huge chunk of the portfolio.
